body:
`.menuBtn` in `frontend/src/components/TopBar.module.css` is a flex item in a
crowded top bar with no `flex: none` and no explicit width, so it is squeezed
whenever the bar runs out of room. Measured on `main` (not a branch), /app/account:

    390px -> button 22x28, icon 14x20
    360px -> button 20x28, icon 12x20
    320px -> button  8x28, icon  0x20   <- no glyph rendered at all

At 320px (Galaxy Fold folded, and the narrowest width the project checks) the
primary navigation control on mobile is invisible. It is still present and
clickable — PR #1506 guarantees its hit area stays at least 30x44 there — so
this is a discoverability defect, not a dead control.

Not fixed alongside the target-size work because it is not a target-size
problem: the bar genuinely cannot fit brand + search + hamburger + account menu
at 320px, and the squeeze is how it currently copes. Fixing it means choosing
what yields first — most likely dropping `.brandText` below ~360px, since
`.triggerLabel` already hides at 420px and the search already collapses to an
icon button. That is a layout decision, so it wants to be made deliberately
rather than as a side effect.

Related: `/duplicates` and `/admin` are the only two routes that overflow
horizontally at 320px (`.scanBtn` is `white-space: nowrap` at 151px, reaching
352px against a 320px viewport; `.userActions` reaches 323px). Same width, same
class of problem, likely worth one pass together.

Method + full inventory: `notes/UI-SWEEP-INVENTORY.md` (outer workspace).
title: The mobile hamburger renders no glyph at 320px
